text:
incident-bot: 🔥 PagerDuty alert fired PD-89217 — inference-queue backlog > 95% for cell 'us-west-2-a' (autoscaler not keeping up)
pagerduty: PD-89217 assigned to @maya
maya: acked — i'm on it. seeing huge queue depth, latency spiking. first pass: confirm scope and impact
devon: looking at metrics now — autoscaler health shows failed provisioning attempts, kube API 429s, spot pools constrained
ingrid: any customer-facing errors? support dashboard showing increased 503s for /v1/generate in the last 3m
maya: yes, 503 rate ~3.8% over baseline, p95 latency up from 120ms -> 820ms. a few long tails hitting 2-3s
ben: stack: ingress -> router -> dispatcher -> inference queue -> workers. backlog is piling at dispatcher level
devon: logs: dispatcher shows repeated "enqueue timeout" and worker pod churn. snippet:
```
2026-03-15T14:12:08Z dispatcher ERROR enqueue timeout queue_size=12487
2026-03-15T14:12:09Z autoscaler WARN spinup failed reason=kube-apiserver-429
```
maya: trying a manual scale override to add reserved nodes for the inference pool
devon: +1 — do `kubectl scale` on deployment inference-worker-prod --replicas=40, but autoscaler may fight it, set annotation to disable autoscale
maya: running:
```
kubectl patch deployment inference-worker-prod -n redwood --patch '{"spec":{"replicas":40}}'
kubectl annotate deployment inference-worker-prod redwood/disable-autoscale=true --overwrite
```
maya: applied patch. workers count climbing, new pods in Pending for a bit then Running
ingrid: metrics updating — queue depth dropping slowly from 12.5k -> 9.3k
ben: still seeing a few evictions on the spot fleet — provider spot reclaim spikes earlier this hour
devon: mitigations: 1) manual scale (done), 2) switch new nodes to on-demand for this pool, 3) temporarily increase dispatch timeout to reduce enqueue pressure
maya: initiating provider request to convert 10 nodes to on-demand in us-west-2-a
pagerduty: PD-89217 escalated to SRE lead per escalation policy (no ack from lead after 2m)
maya: @devon can you bump dispatch timeout? config lives in router configmap
devon: editing configmap now, patching `router.dispatch.timeout` from 50ms -> 200ms
devon: applied — restarting router pods one at a time
ingrid: customer impact note: majority of traffic degraded to higher latency, small percentage 503s. Sending triage to support to update status page
maya: support notified, status page draft: "Degraded generation latency and intermittent errors affecting some requests in US-WEST region. Engineers are mitigating."
ben: watch: autoscaler controller logs show many scale decisions throttled due to quota checks. need quota bump for project redwood-prod
devon: opened quota request with cloud ops (ticket CO-5561). Meanwhile converted 6 spot -> on-demand, new nodes stabilized
maya: queue depth now 3.2k and falling, p95 at ~360ms, 503s back down to 0.6%
ingrid: good — keeping PD open until fully normalized and autoscaler root cause identified
maya: follow-ups: 1) postmortem to capture autoscaler misread of cluster quota, 2) add runbook step to auto-fallback to on-demand for critical pools, 3) tweak dispatch timeout heuristics
devon: note for postmortem — reproduce scenario with synthetic load + simulated spot churn
pagerduty: PD-89217 acknowledged by SRE lead @ben
maya: thanks. i'll keep monitoring for 30m then move to incident review channel
ben: leaving a short handoff: monitoring alarms tuned, manual overrides removed (removed disable-autoscale annotation), autoscaler resumed and nodes stable
maya: closing loop — system healthy for now, follow-up ticket created INF-3289 for autoscaler throttling analysis :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident PD-89217 status: acknowledged -> resolved (action taken).
